name: DIGS (Distribution-Informed Gaussian Splatting)
definition: A training-free framework for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation that decouples instance discovery from linguistic naming. It uses a distribution-informed per-Gaussian representation to maintain multi-peaked label distributions at boundaries, enabling clean instance boundaries via late-argmax rendering and a class-agnostic instance ontology via a bidirectional state machine.
summary: DIGS is a training-free 3D segmentation framework that decouples instance discovery from linguistic naming by maintaining multi-peaked label distributions at object boundaries to solve boundary ambiguity.
